patient.name: Daniel O'Connor
patient.complaint: Red, scaly patches on his elbows, knees and scalp, much worse over 2 months
background: Started propranolol for anxiety 3 months ago
Smokes 15 a day; drinks about 30 units a week

diagnosis.exam: Expect 'Which is the most likely diagnosis?' with well-demarcated silvery plaques on extensor surfaces, drop-like lesions after a sore throat (guttate), or nail pitting with DIP arthritis.

points: Daniel, 38: thick **red, scaly patches** on elbows and knees.
Smokes and drinks heavily; father had similar skin.

steps.lead: Daniel's thick, scaly plaques come from **keratinocytes dividing far too fast**, driven by the immune system.

points: **Well-demarcated**, coin-shaped plaques with **silvery scale** on both extensors.
Plaques along the hairline and lower back.
Fingernails: **pits** and one nail lifting off its bed.

steps.lead: Daniel has classic **plaque psoriasis**: extensor silvery plaques, a positive **Auspitz sign**, **nail pitting** and **onycholysis**.
Daniel's flare has a clear culprit: **propranolol**. Smoking, alcohol and cold weather add to it.

steps.q: Which of Daniel's medicines or habits is LEAST likely to be worsening his psoriasis?
steps.r: **Beta-blockers, lithium**, aspirin, steroid withdrawal, smoking and alcohol trigger flares. Paracetamol does not.

steps.lead: If Daniel were a teenager with small **drop-shaped** lesions 2 to 4 weeks after **strep throat**, this would be **guttate** psoriasis. New plaques on scratches are **Koebner**.

points: Daniel's left index finger end-joint is swollen and stiff.
Several DIP joints ache in the morning.
Whole of one toe is swollen: a 'sausage' digit.

steps.lead: Swollen **DIP joints** with nail disease: Daniel has **psoriatic arthritis**. He also carries higher **cardiovascular** and metabolic risk.

steps.text: Psoriatic arthritis can come **before** the rash. A swollen DIP joint with nail pitting, or **dactylitis**, should make you look for psoriasis on the scalp and natal cleft.

investigation.exam: Expect 'Which is the most appropriate investigation?' where the answer is usually none (clinical), with biopsy only if atypical, and PASI or BSA above 10 defining moderate-to-severe disease.

steps.q: Daniel's plaques are textbook. What confirms the diagnosis?
steps.r: Psoriasis is a **clinical diagnosis**. Biopsy is only for atypical or uncertain cases.

steps.lead: Daniel needs **no biopsy**: well-demarcated silvery extensor plaques with nail pitting are diagnostic.
Severity decides Daniel's treatment. He is scored with **PASI** and **body surface area**; above **10** is moderate to severe.

visual.title: Daniel's PASI score
visual.label: Daniel 14
visual.caption: PASI above 10 (or BSA above 10%) is moderate to severe: escalate beyond topicals.

steps.title: Baseline bloods before possible systemic treatment
steps.text: Raised lipids and HbA1c fit psoriasis-linked **metabolic syndrome**. A raised ALT with alcohol matters before methotrexate.
Remember **10 and 10**: PASI above 10 or BSA above 10% is moderate-to-severe psoriasis and the trigger for phototherapy.

management.exam: Expect 'Which is the most appropriate initial management?': potent steroid plus vitamin D analogue first, phototherapy when PASI is above 10, then methotrexate or ciclosporin, then biologics; guttate needs only reassurance.

steps.title: The psoriasis treatment ladder
nodes: Potent topical steroid + vitamin D analogue, once daily
Vitamin D analogue twice daily (with steroid)
steps.caption: Climb a rung when control is inadequate or PASI/BSA is above 10.

steps.lead: Daniel starts **calcipotriol plus betamethasone** once daily, with a potent steroid for his scalp. Stopping propranolol helps too.

steps.q: After 8 weeks Daniel is only a little better. What is the next topical step?
o: Vitamin D analogue twice daily with the steroid
steps.r: If not controlled, increase the **vitamin D analogue to twice daily** alongside the steroid. Oral steroids cause rebound flares.

steps.lead: Daniel's PASI is still **14**, so he is offered **narrowband UVB**. Warn him about sunburn, skin ageing and skin cancer.
With psoriatic arthritis too, Daniel may need **methotrexate**, but his **alcohol** and raised ALT must be addressed first.
If methotrexate failed, Daniel would move to a **biologic**: adalimumab or **ustekinumab**. PUVA is an older option with **SCC** risk.
Once controlled, Daniel keeps **calcipotriol** as his long-term maintenance treatment.

visual.title: Daniel's PASI over a year
visual.caption: Each rung of the ladder brought the PASI down. Below 10 he no longer counts as moderate to severe.

steps.lead: Daniel's care follows **NICE CG153**, using the **PASI/BSA** thresholds to decide escalation.

steps.text: **Acitretin** is teratogenic: avoid in women who may become pregnant. **Ciclosporin** works fast and suits women of childbearing age.

science.exam: Expect applied questions: the Th17/IL-23 axis and keratinocyte turnover, the Auspitz and Koebner mechanisms, molecular mimicry in guttate psoriasis, and how ustekinumab works.

steps.lead: Daniel's **Th17/IL-23** driven inflammation speeds keratinocyte turnover from 28 days to 3 to 5, so cells reach the surface immature (**parakeratosis**).

visual.title: Keratinocyte turnover time
visual.label: Daniel about 4
visual.caption: Cells pile up before they mature, producing thick silvery scale.

steps.title: From immune signal to plaque
steps.caption: Biologics break this chain at IL-23 or TNF.

steps.lead: Daniel bled from tiny points when his scale was lifted: thin epidermis over **dilated, tortuous capillaries**.
**Ustekinumab** blocks the **p40** subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23, cutting off the Th17 pathway driving Daniel's plaques.
New plaques along a scratch on Daniel's arm would be the **Koebner phenomenon**: trauma switches on the same inflammation locally.

steps.q: Why does guttate psoriasis follow a streptococcal sore throat?
o: Direct strep infection of the skin
Molecular mimicry between strep antigens and keratinocyte proteins
steps.r: **Molecular mimicry**: T cells primed against strep antigens cross-react with keratinocytes.

steps.lead: That is why a teenager can erupt in drop-shaped plaques **2 to 4 weeks** after tonsillitis.
Daniel's high cholesterol and HbA1c are not coincidence: **chronic systemic inflammation** links psoriasis to cardiovascular disease.

mcq.r: **Auspitz**: pinpoint bleeding when scale is removed.

steps.x: **C. Plaque psoriasis.** Well-demarcated silvery extensor plaques + nail pits.

technique.stem: A 16 year old girl has a 1 week history of many small, red, scaly, drop-shaped spots over her trunk and thighs. She had a sore throat 3 weeks ago. She is otherwise well.

technique.stem: A 50 year old man with plaque psoriasis has scale gently scraped from a plaque on his knee. Small points of bleeding appear.
technique.q: Which is the most likely explanation for this sign?
o: Thin suprapapillary epidermis over dilated dermal capillaries

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: That is the Nikolsky sign in pemphigus.
That is Darier's sign.

practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Well-demarcated plaques with silvery scale on extensors and lower back are plaque psoriasis. Eczema is poorly demarcated and flexural.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Poorly demarcated flexural rash.
Coin-shaped but crusted and weeping, not silvery.

Not a recognised trigger.
Not a trigger.
Not a recognised trigger.

practice.stem:
A 49 year old man with plaque psoriasis has a 4 month history of pain and swelling in the end joints of several fingers. One toe is diffusely swollen. His nails are pitted. His temperature is 36.9°C.

Investigations:
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: DIP joint arthritis with dactylitis and nail pitting in a seronegative patient with psoriasis is psoriatic arthritis. RA spares the DIPs.

DIP arthritis, dactylitis, nail pitting, seronegative.

practice.stem: A 33 year old woman with plaque psoriasis had an appendicectomy 3 weeks ago. New well-demarcated scaly red plaques have appeared exactly along her surgical scar. Her temperature is 36.7°C and pulse rate 76 bpm.
practice.q: Which is the most likely explanation for the new lesions?
practice.e: New psoriatic lesions at sites of skin trauma are the Koebner phenomenon. Nikolsky sign is skin shearing in blistering disease.

steps.x: New psoriatic plaques at a site of skin trauma.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Urtication when mastocytosis lesions are rubbed.
A wheal along a line of stroking.
Skin shearing in pemphigus or SJS.
Lacy white lines on lichen planus papules.

practice.stem:

glossary.Psoriasis: Chronic immune-mediated skin disease with thick, scaly plaques from fast keratinocyte turnover.
glossary.Plaque psoriasis: The commonest type: well-demarcated red plaques with silvery scale on extensors.
glossary.Guttate psoriasis: Many small drop-shaped plaques appearing 2 to 4 weeks after a streptococcal infection.
glossary.Keratinocyte: The main cell of the epidermis, which matures as it moves to the surface.
glossary.Parakeratosis: Retained nuclei in the outer skin layer from incomplete maturation; gives psoriatic scale.
glossary.Well-demarcated: With a sharp, clear edge between affected and normal skin.
glossary.Extensor surfaces: The outer side of joints, such as the backs of elbows and fronts of knees.
glossary.Auspitz sign: Pinpoint bleeding when psoriatic scale is scraped off.
glossary.Koebner phenomenon: New lesions appearing at sites of skin trauma such as scratches or scars.
glossary.Nail pitting: Small dents in the nail surface, typical of psoriasis.
glossary.Onycholysis: Painless separation of the nail from its nail bed.
glossary.Dactylitis: Swelling of a whole finger or toe ('sausage digit'), typical of psoriatic arthritis.
glossary.Psoriatic arthritis: Inflammatory, usually seronegative arthritis linked to psoriasis, classically affecting DIP joints.
glossary.DIP: Distal interphalangeal joint, the end joint of a finger or toe.
glossary.Metabolic syndrome: Cluster of central obesity, high blood pressure, high glucose and abnormal lipids.
glossary.PASI: Psoriasis Area and Severity Index; above 10 means moderate-to-severe disease.
glossary.BSA: Body surface area affected; above 10% means moderate-to-severe psoriasis.
glossary.Calcipotriol: Topical vitamin D analogue that slows keratinocyte growth.
glossary.Vitamin D analogue: Topical drug like calcipotriol that reduces keratinocyte proliferation.
glossary.Betamethasone: Potent topical corticosteroid, combined with calcipotriol in psoriasis.
glossary.Narrowband UVB: Phototherapy with a narrow band of ultraviolet B light for moderate-to-severe psoriasis.
glossary.Phototherapy: Treatment of skin disease with ultraviolet light.
glossary.PUVA: Psoralen plus UVA photochemotherapy for severe psoriasis; raises squamous cell carcinoma risk.
glossary.Methotrexate: Antifolate systemic drug for severe psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis; teratogenic and hepatotoxic.
glossary.Ciclosporin: Calcineurin inhibitor that acts fast in psoriasis; can harm kidneys and raise blood pressure.
glossary.Acitretin: Oral retinoid for severe psoriasis; teratogenic and causes dry mucous membranes.
glossary.Biologic: An antibody-based drug targeting a specific immune molecule.
glossary.Adalimumab: Anti-TNF-alpha monoclonal antibody used for severe psoriasis.
glossary.Ustekinumab: Monoclonal antibody against the p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23.
glossary.Th17: T-helper 17 cells, which release IL-17 and drive psoriatic inflammation.
glossary.IL-23: Cytokine that maintains Th17 cells; a key driver of psoriasis.
glossary.Molecular mimicry: When microbial antigens resemble self proteins so immune cells attack both.
glossary.Lithium: Mood stabiliser for bipolar disorder; a classic trigger of psoriasis flares.
glossary.Beta-blockers: Drugs such as propranolol that block adrenaline receptors; can trigger psoriasis.
glossary.ASO titre: Antistreptolysin O antibody level, raised after a recent streptococcal infection.
